text: Within a generation, a machine in a port town could make a block of ice for less than it cost to ship one across the sea. The houses on the lake stood empty for a few winters. Then they were taken down and sold for their timber.
strengths: answers how the trade ended in one plain sentence of cause
no verdict on the people or the industry
ends on a physical fact rather than a reflection
weaknesses: relies on the film having made the lake houses familiar
the closing sentence opens on then, which works once and should not become the film's way of ending sequences
spokenRhythm: One long sentence that carries the cause, then two shorter ones that let the consequence settle.
narrativeFunction: Closes a film about a natural-ice business by showing how quietly it was made obsolete.
whyItWorks: It answers the film's question with a reason a listener can follow, then lets the buildings disappear without commentary. There is no summary, no lesson and no last flourish, so the final fact is allowed to do the work.

text: When the oil had been sold and the voyage's costs taken out, the green hand's share came to a little under thirty dollars. He had been away for three years. His bill at the outfitter's, for the clothes and tobacco he had bought on credit before he sailed, came to slightly more.
strengths: the sum is set beside the years it took to earn
the final sentence delivers the verdict through an account, not an opinion
weaknesses: works best when the film has explained the share system and the term green hand earlier
spokenRhythm: A long sentence to the figure, a short one that gives it scale, and a long one whose last two words carry the blow.
narrativeFunction: Answers what a voyage was worth to the lowest-paid man aboard and ends the film on that answer.
whyItWorks: The listener feels thirty dollars against three years without being told to. The outfitter's bill makes the point dryly and leaves the judgment to the audience. It is quiet, specific and complete.

text: The order was lifted eleven weeks after it was signed. The council's accounts show what it paid the farmers for their produce, down to the penny. The burial register stops in the middle of August, when the clerk who kept it died.
strengths: sets a precise record beside a missing one
the cost in lives is shown through an absence in the sources
no sentence tells the listener what to feel
weaknesses: needs the film to have set up both the quarantine order and the register
spokenRhythm: Three sentences of growing length, the last one turning on its final clause.
narrativeFunction: Ends a film about a town's quarantine by measuring what the record kept and what it lost.
whyItWorks: The contrast between accounts kept to the penny and a register that simply stops says more about the summer than any description of grief. The reason it stops is given as a plain fact and the film ends there.

text: They never reached the pole. They came home with forty notebooks of weather readings, which sat in a cupboard at the society's rooms for decades. For that stretch of coast, those readings are still the earliest weather record anyone has.
strengths: states the failure plainly before the consolation
the neglect of the notebooks is told without complaint
the final claim is narrow and checkable, one coast and one kind of record
weaknesses: the turn from failure to legacy is a familiar shape and must not be over-sold in the reading
spokenRhythm: A five-word opener, a long middle sentence, and a medium close.
narrativeFunction: Answers whether the expedition achieved anything and closes on what actually lasted.
whyItWorks: It does not dress the failure up. The notebooks in a cupboard keep the legacy modest and believable, and the final sentence claims only what the film could support.

text: The relief committee closed its books in the spring. It had fed the district through one winter on money raised by subscription. What was left went back to the subscribers, and came to a little over a penny for every pound they had given.
strengths: the achievement is stated once and not praised
the remainder is measured against each giver's own pound, so its smallness is felt
ends on what the committee did, not on what it meant
weaknesses: the listener has to work out that a penny in the pound means almost everything was spent
quiet enough to be lost under closing music
spokenRhythm: Three sentences that lengthen in turn, the last one ending on the small sum.
narrativeFunction: Closes a film about famine relief by showing how completely the money went where it was meant to go.
whyItWorks: Instead of calling the committee careful, it reports the last thing the committee did with the money. Setting the remainder against each subscriber's pound gives the figure a scale anyone can feel, and the film can stop there.

text: The branch line closed to passengers in its ninety-first year. By then the train often ran with fewer than a dozen people aboard. On the last day it was full, and the porter had to turn people away at the gate.
strengths: the irony sits in the facts and the narration never names it
the decline gets one plain sentence instead of a lament
ends on an action at the gate, not on a reflection
weaknesses: an ending built on irony needs a film that has not leaned on irony throughout
spokenRhythm: A medium statement of the closure, a shorter line for the decline, and a longer close that ends on the porter.
narrativeFunction: Ends a film about a rural railway on the day the people who had stopped using it came to see it go.
whyItWorks: The audience sees the contradiction for itself, and nothing tells them whether to find it sad or funny. The porter turning people away carries both at once, so the narration can stop on it.
